title: Support Shiny UI inside of `chat_append()` and `markdown_stream()`
description:
This PR adds support for the content of a message provided to `chat_append()` or `markdown_stream()` to include Shiny UI, and moreover, if that UI includes output or input bindings, they are bound to the server session.

This means, among other things, you can now display things like `{htmlwidgets}` and collect user input from things like a [select input](https://shiny.posit.co/py/components/inputs/select-single/). Here are a couple basic examples:


<details>
<summary>Output example</summary>


```R
library(shiny)
library(shinychat)
library(bslib)
library(plotly)

welcome <- list(
  list(
    "**Hello! Here is a statically rendered widget**",
    plot_ly(x = 1, y = 1, mode = "text", text = "Statically rendered widget")
  ),
  list(
    "**And here is an output binding**",
    plotlyOutput("plt")
  )
)

ui <- page_fillable(
  title = "Hello widgets in chat",
  fillable_mobile = TRUE,
  chat_ui("chat", messages = welcome)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  observeEvent(input$chat_user_input, {
    chat_append("chat", paste("You said:", input$chat_user_input))
  })

  output$plt <- renderPlotly({
    plot_ly(x = 1, y = 1, mode = "text", text = "Dynamically rendered widget")
  })

}


shinyApp(ui, server)

```

</details>



<details>
<summary>Input example</summary>


```R
library(ellmer)
library(shiny)
library(shinychat)
library(bslib)
library(plotly)


welcome <- list(
  list(
    "**Hello! How would you like me to respond?**",
    selectInput("tone", "", choices = c("Happy", "Sad"))
  )
)

ui <- page_fillable(
  title = "Hello input bindings in chat",
  fillable_mobile = TRUE,
  chat_ui("chat", messages = welcome)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  chat <- chat_ollama(model = "llama3.2")

  observeEvent(input$chat_user_input, {
    stream <- chat$stream_async(input$chat_user_input)
    chat_append("chat", stream)
  })

  observeEvent(input$tone, {
    chat$set_system_prompt(paste("You are a terse and", input$tone, "assistant."))
  })

}


shinyApp(ui, server)

```

</details>

fix(markdown-stream): decide auto-scroll pinning before content grows
description:
Fixes posit-dev/py-shiny#2378.

## The bug

`useAutoScroll` recomputes `stickToBottom` **only** inside its `scroll` handler, and that handler reads geometry when the event is *delivered*, not when the scroll happened. Browsers dispatch scroll events asynchronously — on Firefox from a paint tick that can lag under load — so a content chunk can grow `scrollHeight` in the gap.

When it does, the user's at-bottom position reads as:

- not `isAtBottom` — the comparison is against the **grown** height
- not `isScrollingUp` — the user scrolled *down*

Neither branch fires, so `stickToBottom` stays `false`. Nothing else sets the flag and no further scroll events arrive, so the stream **silently stops following new content while still appearing pinned**. It never recovers for the life of the element.

This is the root cause of a py-shiny CI flake whose failure geometry was byte-identical across three weeks and an intervening test-side fix — the tell that the stall point was structural rather than a timing wobble.

## The fix

Add `repinIfAtBottom()` to `useAutoScroll` and call it from `MarkdownStream.appendContent` immediately before `setContent`. At that moment the DOM still holds the pre-growth `scrollHeight`, so "is the user at the bottom?" is unambiguous and needs no event.

It only ever **engages**, never disengages. That asymmetry is load-bearing: chunks routinely arrive while the previous chunk's smooth scroll is still animating, so "not at the bottom" at apply time does not mean the user scrolled away. Disengaging remains the scroll handler's job, where `isScrollingUp` is a genuine user-intent signal.

## Verification

Reproduced first, against py-shiny's existing `MarkdownStream/auto_scroll` app, by delaying delivery of shinychat's scroll callback by 400 ms (emulating a lagging paint tick) while leaving the test's own listener undelayed:

```js
window.__delayScroll = true;
const origAdd = EventTarget.prototype.addEventListener;
EventTarget.prototype.addEventListener = function (type, cb, opts) {
  if (type === "scroll" && window.__delayScroll && typeof cb === "function") {
    return origAdd.call(this, type, (...a) => setTimeout(() => cb(...a), 400), opts);
  }
  return origAdd.call(this, type, cb, opts);
};
```

| | `scrollTop` | `scrollHeight` | `clientHeight` |
|---|---|---|---|
| py-shiny CI failure (both occurrences) | 1998 | 2816 | 258 |
| Repro on `main` | **1998** | **2816** | **258** |
| Repro on this branch | **2558** (= bottom) | 2816 | 258 |

Also checked:

- `npm run test` — 691 pass, 0 fail; `npm run lint` clean.
- New unit tests: the late-scroll-event regression, the mid-animation guard (must not disengage), and the negative case (must not re-pin while the user is scrolled away).
- New `MarkdownStream` test asserting pinnedness is settled *before* the appended chunk reaches the DOM — ordering is the whole point, so it's worth pinning down.
- py-shiny's full `MarkdownStream` playwright suite passes on Firefox and Chromium against the rebuilt asset.
- Fast-stream regression check (200 chunks at 10 ms) ends flush at the bottom on both browsers, identical to the `main` baseline — the engage-only asymmetry holds up in a real browser.

`js/dist` + `pkg-py` / `pkg-r` assets are rebuilt and synced per `CLAUDE.md`. Changelog entries to follow in a second commit once this has a PR number.

title: feat: render tool calls as quiet, groupable rows
description:
A single agentic turn that called three tools produced three full cards — header,
arguments, result body, stacked. The transcript read as tool machinery with an answer
buried somewhere in it. Tool activity is *subordinate* to the assistant's answer, and
it should read that way.

Tool calls now render as a **quiet one-line row**: an identity glyph, the tool's
title, a short peek at the result, and a chevron. Calls to the same tool in one
tool-calling phase collapse into a single row with a `×N` badge. Everything that used
to be on screen is still one click away.

```
Before                              After
┌────────────────────────────┐
│ ▸ Searched the docs        │      ◇ Thought for 2s
│   query: "net revenue"     │      · Searched the docs ×3            ▸
├────────────────────────────┤      · Read page: handbook.internal    ▸
│ ▸ Searched the docs        │
│   query: "discounts"       │
├────────────────────────────┤
│ ▸ Read page                │
│   url: handbook.internal…  │
└────────────────────────────┘
```

Layered onto the existing request → result → streaming protocol, not a rewrite of it.
**Both languages, one behaviour.**

## Three disclosure tiers

1. **The resting row** — dimmed, `0.8em`, normal weight. Quiet by default.
2. **The per-call list** — for a grouped row, revealed on expand.
3. **The full card** — arguments and result body, exactly what shipped before.

A single-call row skips tier 2 and opens straight to the card. The card's own header
is hidden in the morph, so the row *becomes* the header; fullscreen keeps it. Row
space is reserved identically for the single and aggregated shapes, so a call landing
and promoting a row to `×2` causes no layout jump.

## New API

**Chat-level**, on `chat_ui()` / `Chat.ui()`:

- **`tool_grouping`** — `"tool"` (default) groups calls to the same tool within a
  turn's tool-calling phase, order-independent rather than only consecutive; `"all"`
  groups every call in the phase; `"none"` is one card per call, the old behaviour.
  It's also a **live custom-element attribute** — changing it re-routes the transcript
  already on screen with no server round-trip.
- **`icon_assistant=False`** removes the assistant icon and its streaming dots.

**Per-result**, on `ToolResultDisplay` / `tool_result_display()`:

- **`label`** — the per-call identifying value, rendered as `{title}: {label}`. A
  filename, a query, a URL.
- **`value_preview`** — a terse display-only peek: `"1,204 rows"`, `"3.1 kB · 200 OK"`.

**Per-tool**, as a definition-level annotation next to `title` / `icon`:

- **`grouping`** — a per-tool override of the chat-level mode. Grouping is a per-tool
  decision, not a per-result one. Chat-level `"none"` deliberately beats the
  annotation: it means grouping is *off*, so a tool can opt out of the chat's choice
  of how to group but can't opt back into grouping the app switched off.

R also gains an exported **`tool_result_display()`** constructor, matching Python's
`ToolResultDisplay`. Bare named lists still work and are promoted internally.

## Fully custom tool UI now works end to end

Both packages already let an app render a tool result as *entirely custom UI* — R via
a `contents_shinychat()` method, Python via a `message_content` handler. That bare
return left **no `<shiny-tool-result>` in the transcript at all**, so nothing could
tell the request had been answered and **the request row spun forever.**

shinychat now wraps that output in a real `<shiny-tool-result>` itself. **No
author-facing API change** — existing apps of this shape are fixed retroactively.
Detection is by artifact-marking rather than by shape, which is what preserves the
extend-vs-replace distinction: an author who follows the documented `S7::super()`
pattern (mutate `res$value`, return shinychat's own card) correctly reads as *not*
custom.

Turning that bypass into a supported path is what let an imperative wire action be
deleted: whether a request has been superseded is now **derived from content**, so it
replays identically through preload, bookmark restore, and history replay instead of
depending on a signal that only exists live.

## Behaviour change worth calling out

**The client no longer conjugates tool titles.** The `"Running {title}"` /
`"{title} failed"` template is gone. Present → past now comes entirely from two
author-supplied strings: the tool's definition title (static, present tense) while it
runs, and the result title (dynamic, past tense) once the first result lands, latched
one-way so a settled row never reverts.

If a title reads oddly while running now that the automatic prefix is gone, write an
explicit present-tense definition title (`"Running R code"`) and optionally a
past-tense result title (`"Ran R code"`). Failures are a separate status cue — a
`failed` / `N failed` note and icon — rather than text appended to the title. The
count is always a separate `×N` badge, never inline, so **there is no pluralization
or numeral-agreement API at all**; zero new phrasing strings ship here.

## How it works

Grouping is a **pure pre-render content router**, not React-tree grouping. One pass
parses tool custom-element attributes out of the raw content string and rewrites the
message into typed blocks, where a run of tool elements uninterrupted by prose becomes
one `tool_loop` carrying a group model. The per-element bridges shrank to leaf
renderers.

The reason it's shaped that way is **replayability**: history restore re-runs the same
pure function over the same content and reconstructs identical grouping, independent
of render or mount order. React-tree grouping is simpler but render-order-dependent,
so restore and live streaming would disagree. Because the router is pure in
`(blocks, grouping, role)` and a loop retains the raw slice it was parsed from,
changing `tool_grouping` at runtime is just a re-route — which is where the live
attribute comes from, for free.

## Tests

~5,500 added test lines, roughly 59% of the diff:

- **JS** — `js/tests/chat/ToolGroup.test.tsx` (+1,768) and large additions to
  `state.test.ts` and `ChatMessage.test.tsx`. 845 passing.
- **Python** — new `pkg-py/tests/pytest/test_tool_condensed_view.py` (+721), plus a
  `tools/custom_output` Playwright app.
- **R** — new `test-tool-custom-output.R` (+399) and substantial
  `test-contents_shinychat.R` additions.

A structural test pins the invariant that a **homogeneous group renders byte-identical
markup to the pre-segment implementation**, so the multi-tool header work can't
silently change the common case.

## Reviewing this

- **Skip `87f38c5`** — a mechanical `ruff format` pass touching 27 files, 25 of them
  unrelated to this feature. Verified formatting-only (identical ASTs once docstrings
  are normalized; the docstring diffs are `docstring-code-format`). Isolated in its
  own commit precisely so it can be skipped. `ruff check` had been passing
  independently, which is how the drift went unnoticed.
- **`2bc5cb7` and `46eaab0` cancel out.** A "thinking-lift" feature — hoisting a
  loop's reasoning into one merged row above its calls at `tool_grouping="all"` — was
  built, tested in a browser, and reverted the same day: hoisting rearranges the
  transcript into an order the model never produced, so a thought that plainly
  followed one tool and motivated the next appeared to precede both. Neither commit's
  code is in the final diff. Kept in history because the reasoning is worth having.
  Thinking now renders in its linear position at every mode and breaks the loop, so
  `"all"` aggregates only genuinely adjacent calls.
- **Two `impeccable` findings resolved by deletion, not rewriting.** A `max-height`
  transition on the tool card body turned out to be **inert** — expanded leaves
  `max-height: none`, which CSS can't interpolate with the collapsed `0`, so only the
  `opacity` half ever animated. And a `padding-block` transition on the thinking body
  was redundant with the `grid-template-rows` animation its parent already runs over
  the same duration. Both removed; nothing changes visually.

## Deliberately not in this PR

Each of these wants its own issue:

- **Serializing rendered UI into R's bookmark state.** R replays *turns*, never a
  snapshot, so it has neither an `html_deps` round-trip nor UI serialization. Includes
  the open question of whether R's **history replay** path — the default, and probably
  the higher-impact half — is covered by the same fix.
- **A server-side `update_tool_grouping()`** mirroring `update_cancel` /
  `update_upload`. The client half ships here; only the documented server API waits.
- **Hoisting the router to transcript scope**, which collides with #269's
  sibling/edit navigation.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion` doesn't cover the tool chevrons** — a pre-existing
  one-line gap in `chat-tools.scss`.
- Plus: dropping `merge_ellmer_turn_group()`, unflattening `message_content(Turn)`,
  servers not emitting `content-type`, and a latent validation-escalation issue in
  Python's `ToolResultDisplay`.

title: feat(pkg-r): restore chat's displayed UI faithfully from bookmarks
description:
## Summary

Stacked on #287 — merge that first; this diff shows only the commits on top of it.

- `chat_restore()` bookmarks currently re-derive the displayed chat UI from the LLM's turns on restore. Any display-only transformation applied between "message received" and "message shown" (e.g. a `transform_assistant_response` that only affects rendering) is lost, so the restored page can look different from what the user actually saw when they bookmarked it.
- Bookmarks (server store only) now capture the browser's own displayed-message snapshot and replay that directly on restore, so the restored UI is byte-faithful to what was shown. Falls back to the turn-derived UI for `bookmarkStore = "url"` and for bookmarks saved before this existed, with a warning if a saved snapshot can't be read back (e.g. written by an incompatible shinychat version).
- The response-bookmark trigger moves from "stream just ended" to "the browser has echoed the finished reply," since bookmarking at stream-end could persist a snapshot missing the reply the client hadn't reported back yet.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` (js) — 713 passing
- [x] `devtools::test()` (R) — 676 passing

## Known follow-ups, not addressed here

- The user-submission guard that prevents a startup/restore replay from minting a spurious bookmark only covers the *first* replay window. An app pairing `chat_restore()` with `chat_enable_history()` can still mint one bookmark per echo when switching conversations after the user has already submitted once this session.
- `markdown_stream()` lost its own bookmark-on-response trigger in this branch with no replacement (it never emits a `_messages` echo, so it can't use the new trigger). Flagging since it's a behavior removal, not obviously dead code.

title: fix(pkg-py): degrade gracefully on a malformed bookmarked message
description:
## Summary

A bookmark written by an incompatible shinychat version (or otherwise malformed) currently makes `Chat._restore_bookmark_message()` raise. That aborts the caller's restore loop entirely — Shiny's generic `on_restore` error handling just shows a banner, it doesn't resume the loop — so every message *after* the bad one silently disappears too, not just the bad one. Now it warns and skips just the one malformed message, restoring everything else.

## Test plan

- [x] New test seeds one malformed message between two valid ones and asserts both valid ones still restore, with a warning raised for the bad one.

title: security: validate reported html against a ledger of what the server sent
description:
## Summary

- The browser reports its own message snapshot back to the server (`input$<id>_messages` / `input[f"{id}_messages"]`), and that report is currently trusted for `content_type: "html"` segments and `htmlDeps` objects. That report is persisted verbatim into the already-shipped chat-history store, and is the input a future bookmark-restore feature would persist into shareable server-bookmark state. A forged report is a stored-script vector against whoever later opens that history or bookmark — the raw-HTML sinks it reaches (`innerHTML`, and the tool cards' `icon`/`footer`/`value` attributes via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`) don't distinguish content the server actually sent from content the client merely claims it sent.
- Closes that gap with a server-side ledger of what was actually sent, built by mirroring the client's own chunk-merging (the browser only ever reports a *settled* message, never an in-flight one, so there's exactly one string per segment to recognize). The browser's report is validated against the ledger at the input-handler boundary — before `session$input$<id>_messages` is ever read by anything downstream — so history saves, and any future consumer of the same input, get the protection automatically. Untrusted html degrades to inert markdown; untrusted dependencies are dropped and trusted ones are swapped for the server's own copy.
- Same boundary added in Python (`_html_trust.py`), which had the identical gap in `messages_input_value()`.

## Test plan

- [x] `devtools::test()` (R) — 684 passing, including an adversarial pair that forges a `_messages` report, sanitizes it, and asserts the replay primitive shared by history-switch and bookmark-restore never re-emits `"html"` or a dependency the server didn't send
- [x] `uv run pytest` (py) — 372 passing, including an end-to-end case that drives a real `Chat.append_message(HTML(...))` through the actual send path and feeds the wire content back through the input handler the way the browser would
- [x] `pyright`, `ruff check` — clean

title: security: escape shinychat's raw-HTML element names in markdown content
description:
## Summary

- Assistant *markdown* that happens to contain the literal text `<shinychat-raw-html>`, `<shiny-tool-request>`, or `<shiny-tool-result>` was rendered as those live custom elements, which write straight to `innerHTML`/`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. No bookmark, no forged input, no feature flag — just model output (e.g. a RAG document, a tool result fetching an untrusted page) repeating one of those names verbatim, which is the standard indirect-prompt-injection shape. Those names are now escaped whenever content renders through the markdown branch, so they display as literal text instead of instantiating a live element.
- Bundled in because the escaping fix would otherwise regress it: `chat_ui(messages=)` (R and Python) was mislabeling htmltools/Shiny UI content as markdown instead of `"html"`. That mislabeling was harmless before (the raw-html wrapper just displayed as odd literal text); once markdown-rendered content escapes that wrapper's name too, the same mislabeling would make widgets in initial chat messages stop rendering entirely. Fixed alongside so the escaping fix doesn't ship a regression.

title: fix(history): preserve file-backed R conversation turns
description:
## Why this matters

File-backed R conversation history can now restore every valid ellmer turn after a reload without changing its R types. Previously, ordinary JSON encoding converted version numbers, vectors, structured JSON values, and missing assistant metadata into incompatible shapes, causing `contents_replay()` to fail.

## What changed

- Persist each recorded turn with `jsonlite::serializeJSON()` inside the existing JSONL envelope and restore it with `jsonlite::unserializeJSON()`.
- Keep `set_turns_recorded()` storage-agnostic instead of repairing decoded values with type-shape heuristics.
- Add layered regression coverage for file storage, server restoration, and a real R Shiny browser session.

No migration path is included because conversation history has not shipped in an R release.

## Additional test coverage

- A file-store test saves real recorded ellmer turns, creates a fresh `FileConversationStore`, appends another turn, restarts again, and verifies the exact recorded values survive both cold starts.
- An R `testServer()` lifecycle test saves an exchange, restores it with fresh client and store instances, continues the conversation, then restores all four turns from a third fresh store while checking structured JSON and missing assistant metadata.
- A Playwright test starts a real R Shiny app, saves and restores a transcript across two page reloads, continues after the first reload, and verifies the final four-message transcript exactly.

title: fix: standardize shiny chat CSS and raw HTML prefixes
description:
Fixes #285
Fixes #286

## Summary
The `shinychat-*` prefix is a natural product-oriented naming choice, so it has gradually slipped into a subset of CSS classes, custom properties, and keyframes. But the established public CSS and DOM convention is `shiny-chat-*`, starting from `<shiny-chat-container>`. This PR corrects that inconsistency by standardizing the public CSS API on `shiny-chat-*`.

- Rename public CSS classes, custom properties, and keyframes from `shinychat-*` to `shiny-chat-*`.
- Add canonical `AGENTS.md` guidance, with `CLAUDE.md` symlinked to it, to reserve `shiny-chat-*` for CSS identifiers and prevent the deprecated prefix from returning.
- Preserve `shinychat-*` for product and integration key names where it remains appropriate, such as package names, `data-shinychat-*` attributes, and browser storage keys.

The raw-HTML island marker was intentionally handled in a separate commit. R and Python now emit `<shiny-chat-raw-html>`, while JavaScript continues to recognize and style legacy `<shinychat-raw-html>` content. The initial reservation was that this marker is serialized in server-to-client content and may appear in restored history; keeping it as a legacy-read alias resolves that compatibility concern while allowing new output to follow the established DOM naming convention. Its separate commit also makes reverting that decision straightforward if needed.

title: fix(chat): preserve scroll when browsing edited branches
description:
## Why this matters

Editing a message creates an alternate branch of the conversation. Before this change, switching between those branches could unexpectedly move the chat viewport: for example, returning from a short edited branch to the original, longer conversation could jump the reader to the bottom even though they had been reading near the top. That makes it difficult to compare earlier messages and responses across versions.

An edit itself should still behave like a new submission: when a user edits an earlier message, the regenerated response belongs at the end of the newly active branch and should be brought into view. Likewise, a server refresh that only updates the "1 / 2" sibling indicator should not move the viewport at all.

## What changed

- Preserve the user's exact scroll position while the chat replaces one sibling branch with another.
- Keep the existing scroll-to-bottom behavior after an edited message is resubmitted and its response is regenerated.
- Ensure passive sibling-metadata refreshes do not override manual scrolling.
- Add Playwright coverage for each of these behaviors in an overflowing conversation.

## Verification

The browser coverage verifies that editing an earlier message scrolls to its regenerated response, while navigating to a sibling branch and receiving a passive sibling-metadata update both leave a manually chosen viewport position intact.
